lec05kp12en-u01-p1-title.name: u01-p1-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p1-title.text: Can the model recognize the same stroke at a new position?

lec05kp12en-u01-p1-bridge.name: u01-p1-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p1-bridge.text: KP11 removed unnecessary freedom. If positions need the same judgment, can they reuse parameters from the start?

lec05kp12en-u01-p1-next-question.name: u01-p1-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p1-next-question.text: What local patch should each position inspect to recognize it?

lec05kp12en-u01-p1-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-shift
lec05kp12en-u01-p1-fig1.text: 相同三格直筆畫在6乘6影像內向右移動兩格，沒有裁掉筆畫。

image.alt: The same three-pixel vertical stroke shifts two columns right inside two six-by-six images without cropping.

lec05kp12en-u01-p1-card1.name: term:Transformation invariance
lec05kp12en-u01-p1-card1.text: **Transformation invariance**: For a specified transformation T, invariance means $c(Tx)=c(x)$. State which transformation is intended.

lec05kp12en-u01-p1-card2.name: u01-p1-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p1-card2.text: The same three-pixel stroke shifts right by two cells without cropping. Its class should stay the same; intermediate arrays need not.

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-title.name: u01-p2-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-title.text: Each position first examines a small local patch

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-bridge.name: u01-p2-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-bridge.text: The same three-pixel stroke shifts without cropping. What local patch should each position inspect to recognize it?

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-next-question.name: u01-p2-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-next-question.text: Can those positions reuse one set of weights?

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-patch
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-fig1.text: 6乘6影像中的3乘3視窗，視窗是單一位置的感受野。

image.alt: An orange three-by-three receptive-field window inside the six-by-six stroke image.

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-card1.name: term:Receptive field
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-card1.text: **Receptive field**: A receptive field is the input region directly visible to a unit; here it is a 3×3 patch.

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-card2.name: u01-p2-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-card2.text: The image is 6×6. A stride-one 3×3 window with no padding has $4\times4=16$ valid positions.

lec05kp12en-u01-p2-card3.name: u01-p2-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p2-card3.text: One position sees nine numbers. Positions see different data but can apply the same rule.

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-title.name: u01-p3-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-title.text: Reuse one set of nine weights at every window

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-bridge.name: u01-p3-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-bridge.text: A receptive field sees nine numbers at each of sixteen positions. Can those positions reuse one set of weights?

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-next-question.name: u01-p3-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-next-question.text: How do we organize scores while retaining positions?

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-kernel
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-fig1.text: 重用的3乘3權重矩陣，中欄為1，其餘為0，偏置為0。

image.alt: Reusable three-by-three kernel with ones in its center column, zeros elsewhere and bias zero.

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-card1.name: term:Weight sharing
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-card1.text: **Weight sharing**: Weight sharing constrains corresponding connections to use one adjustable value, updated as a single parameter.

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-card2.name: term:Kernel
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-card2.text: **Kernel**: A kernel is the weight matrix reused across windows; this example has ones in the middle column, zeros elsewhere and zero bias.

lec05kp12en-u01-p3-card3.name: u01-p3-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p3-card3.text: A patch with middle column $1,1,1$ scores $1\times1+1\times1+1\times1=3$, a score for this local feature only.

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-title.name: u01-p4-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-title.text: Arrange local scores into a feature map

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-bridge.name: u01-p4-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-bridge.text: One reusable set of nine weights gives a local feature score. How do we organize scores while retaining positions?

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-next-question.name: u01-p4-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-next-question.text: Both maxima are three at different locations: is the map itself unchanged?

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-maps
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-fig1.text: 共享同一權重計算兩張4乘4特徵圖，反應跟著平移，最大值都等於3。

image.alt: Two four-by-four response maps using the shared kernel; the maximum value three moves two columns and max pooling stays three.

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-card1.name: term:Feature map
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-card1.text: **Feature map**: A feature map arranges local responses by position; this one is 4×4.

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-card2.name: u01-p4-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-card2.text: The maps show responses before and after image translation using the same weights. Both maxima are 3, at different locations.

lec05kp12en-u01-p4-card3.name: u01-p4-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p4-card3.text: The kernel evaluates local data; it does not automatically discard where the feature occurs.

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-title.name: u01-p5-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-title.text: Shared weights usually make responses move with the input

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-bridge.name: u01-p5-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-bridge.text: The feature map retains local responses by position. Both maxima are three at different locations: is the map itself unchanged?

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-next-question.name: u01-p5-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-next-question.text: How can classification discard position while retaining the feature?

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-maps
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-fig1.text: 共享同一權重計算兩張4乘4特徵圖，反應跟著平移，最大值都等於3。

image.alt: Two four-by-four response maps using the shared kernel; the maximum value three moves two columns and max pooling stays three.

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-card1.name: term:Translation equivariance
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-card1.text: **Translation equivariance**: Translation equivariance means a translated input produces a correspondingly translated response: $F(Tx)=TF(x)$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-card2.name: u01-p5-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-card2.text: F maps an image to a feature map, and T is translation. Usually $F(Tx)\ne F(x)$ because the high-response position changes.

lec05kp12en-u01-p5-card3.name: u01-p5-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p5-card3.text: Integer shifts, stride, padding and boundary conditions must be compatible; cropping can also destroy the correspondence.

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-title.name: u01-p6-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-title.text: Aggregating over position can create an invariant feature

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-bridge.name: u01-p6-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-bridge.text: Translation equivariance gives a correspondingly translated response. How can classification discard position while retaining the feature?

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-next-question.name: u01-p6-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-next-question.text: How many adjustable numbers does sharing also save?

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-maps
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-fig1.text: 共享同一權重計算兩張4乘4特徵圖，反應跟著平移，最大值都等於3。

image.alt: Two four-by-four response maps using the shared kernel; the maximum value three moves two columns and max pooling stays three.

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-card1.name: term:Global max pooling
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-card1.text: **Global max pooling**: Global max pooling retains only $z=\max_{i,j}F(x)_{ij}$ from the feature map.

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-card2.name: u01-p6-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-card2.text: Both images give $z=3$. A later classifier using only z receives the same feature for these two images.

lec05kp12en-u01-p6-card3.name: u01-p6-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p6-card3.text: This checks the example and translations preserving the feature. Pooling loses location and may be inappropriate for precise localization.

lec05kp12en-u01-p7-title.name: u01-p7-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p7-title.text: Sharing across sixteen positions reduces one hundred sixty parameters to ten

lec05kp12en-u01-p7-bridge.name: u01-p7-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p7-bridge.text: Global max pooling retains the same scalar in this example. How many adjustable numbers does sharing also save?

lec05kp12en-u01-p7-next-question.name: u01-p7-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p7-next-question.text: How should one shared value receive updates from every position?

lec05kp12en-u01-p7-card1.name: u01-p7-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p7-card1.text: Without sharing, sixteen positions each have nine weights and one bias: $16\times(9+1)=160$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p7-card2.name: u01-p7-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p7-card2.text: Sharing uses just nine weights and one bias: $9+1=10$. Computation still runs at all sixteen positions.

lec05kp12en-u01-p7-card3.name: u01-p7-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p7-card3.text: The reduction is useful only when the sharing assumption fits the task. Fewer parameters guarantee neither better accuracy nor proportional computation savings.

lec05kp12en-u01-p8-title.name: u01-p8-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p8-title.text: A shared weight accumulates gradients from every use

lec05kp12en-u01-p8-bridge.name: u01-p8-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p8-bridge.text: Sharing uses just nine weights and one bias across sixteen positions. How should one shared value receive updates from every position?

lec05kp12en-u01-p8-next-question.name: u01-p8-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p8-next-question.text: What other approaches complement architecture constraints for transformation stability?

lec05kp12en-u01-p8-card1.name: u01-p8-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p8-card1.text: Let k be a shared weight, r_p the preactivation at position p, x_p its input, and $\delta_p=\partial J/\partial r_p$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p8-card2.name: u01-p8-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p8-card2.text: The chain rule gives $\partial J/\partial k=\sum_p\delta_px_p$. Contributions $0.2\times3$ and $-0.1\times1$ sum to $0.6-0.1=0.5$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p8-card3.name: u01-p8-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p8-card3.text: With learning rate $\eta=0.1$ and k=1, update $k=1-0.1\times0.5=0.95$. Every position then uses 0.95.

lec05kp12en-u01-p9-title.name: u01-p9-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p9-title.text: Invariant features, architectural constraints and augmentation are different routes

lec05kp12en-u01-p9-bridge.name: u01-p9-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p9-bridge.text: A shared weight accumulates gradients from every use. What other approaches complement architecture constraints for transformation stability?

lec05kp12en-u01-p9-next-question.name: u01-p9-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p9-next-question.text: How can architecture also represent products of pixels?

lec05kp12en-u01-p9-card1.name: u01-p9-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p9-card1.text: Choose invariant features, accepting that some useful information may be discarded.

lec05kp12en-u01-p9-card2.name: u01-p9-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p9-card2.text: Constrain architecture with shared weights and suitable aggregation, specifying which computations should match.

lec05kp12en-u01-p9-card3.name: u01-p9-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p9-card3.text: Augment training data with valid transformations; a finite augmented sample usually does not guarantee exact invariance everywhere.

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-title.name: u01-p10-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-title.text: Higher-order networks also weight products of pixels

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-bridge.name: u01-p10-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-bridge.text: Invariant features, architectural constraints and data augmentation can be combined. How can architecture also represent products of pixels?

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-next-question.name: u01-p10-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-next-question.text: Which geometric quantity of a pixel pair is preserved by translation?

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-pair
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-fig1.text: 兩條位移為1,1的線段與同斜率但位移為2,2的線段；同斜率不足以判定純平移。

image.alt: Two segments share displacement one,one; a third has the same slope but displacement two,two, so it is not their pure translation.

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-card1.name: term:Higher-order network
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-card1.text: **Higher-order network**: A higher-order network includes input products in its preactivation, for example $v=b+\sum_i a_ix_i+\sum_{j,k}c_{jk}x_jx_k$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-card2.name: u01-p10-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-card2.text: x_i is a pixel value, a_i a single-pixel weight, c_jk a pair weight, and b a bias, followed by activation $f(v)$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p10-card3.name: u01-p10-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p10-card3.text: For binary pixels the product is one only when both are one. Pair terms can encode joint spatial evidence.

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-title.name: u01-p11-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-title.text: Pure translation preserves displacement, not merely slope

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-bridge.name: u01-p11-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-bridge.text: A higher-order network weights products of pixels. Which geometric quantity of a pixel pair is preserved by translation?

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-next-question.name: u01-p11-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-next-question.text: Which segment property survives rotation and suggests a different tying rule?

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-pair
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-fig1.text: 兩條位移為1,1的線段與同斜率但位移為2,2的線段；同斜率不足以判定純平移。

image.alt: Two segments share displacement one,one; a third has the same slope but displacement two,two, so it is not their pure translation.

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-card1.name: u01-p11-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-card1.text: Translating endpoints by t preserves displacement: $(p_k+t)-(p_j+t)=p_k-p_j$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-card2.name: u01-p11-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-card2.text: The blue pairs both have displacement $(1,1)$ and can share as one displacement group. The orange pair $(2,2)$ has the same slope but is not its translation.

lec05kp12en-u01-p11-card3.name: u01-p11-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p11-card3.text: Matching slopes alone is too coarse. Whole-model invariance also requires compatible single-pixel terms, boundaries and readout.

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-title.name: u01-p12-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-title.text: Rotation preserves length, subject to grid and model conditions

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-bridge.name: u01-p12-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-bridge.text: Pure translation preserves displacement, not merely slope. Which segment property survives rotation and suggests a different tying rule?

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-next-question.name: u01-p12-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-next-question.text: What single shared squared-norm coefficient does the circular model add?

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-pair
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-fig1.text: 兩條位移為1,1的線段與同斜率但位移為2,2的線段；同斜率不足以判定純平移。

image.alt: Two segments share displacement one,one; a third has the same slope but displacement two,two, so it is not their pure translation.

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-card1.name: u01-p12-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-card1.text: Rotation preserves segment length, so equal-length pixel pairs can share second-order coefficients, encoding a geometric prior.

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-card2.name: u01-p12-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-card2.text: On a finite pixel grid, arbitrary rotations require interpolation or cropping. Exact invariance needs compatible transformations, terms and aggregation.

lec05kp12en-u01-p12-card3.name: u01-p12-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p12-card3.text: Sharing can reduce parameters, but the source notes limited adoption of these higher-order methods. Geometry alone is not a performance guarantee.

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-title.name: u01-p13-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-title.text: A shared squared-norm term does not make the whole model invariant

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-bridge.name: u01-p13-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-bridge.text: Rotation preserves segment length, subject to grid conditions. What single shared squared-norm coefficient does the circular model add?

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-next-question.name: u01-p13-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-next-question.text: How did the source postal-code network organize first-order sharing?

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-radius
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-fig1.text: 點1,0與0,1的平方範數都是1；平方範數項對旋轉不變，但不代表整個模型不變。

image.alt: Points one,zero and zero,one both have squared norm one; an invariant term does not imply an invariant full model.

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-card1.name: u01-p13-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-card1.text: $v=b+\sum_i a_ix_i+c\sum_i x_i^2$. One shared coefficient c adds one parameter, not one per pixel.

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-card2.name: u01-p13-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-card2.text: The squared sum is $\|x\|^2$: both $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ give $1^2+0^2=1$. This term is invariant under orthogonal rotations.

lec05kp12en-u01-p13-card3.name: u01-p13-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p13-card3.text: The linear term can differ: for $a=(1,0)$, scores are $b+1+c$ and $b+c$. Reported generalization benefits are cited claims, not proved by this example.

lec05kp12en-u01-p14-title.name: u01-p14-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p14-title.text: The postal-code example combines locality and shared weights

lec05kp12en-u01-p14-bridge.name: u01-p14-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p14-bridge.text: An invariant squared-norm term is not an invariant classifier. How did the source postal-code network organize first-order sharing?

lec05kp12en-u01-p14-next-question.name: u01-p14-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p14-next-question.text: If our toy image grows, which counts change?

lec05kp12en-u01-p14-card1.name: u01-p14-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p14-card1.text: The source describes three hidden layers, with feature maps in the first two. Units receive local windows and corresponding connections share weights within a map.

lec05kp12en-u01-p14-card2.name: u01-p14-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p14-card2.text: It shares the principle of our stroke example, not its architecture. The available description does not justify a full parameter count or accuracy claim.

lec05kp12en-u01-p14-card3.name: u01-p14-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p14-card3.text: First ask which transformations should preserve labels, then choose features, tying rules and readout instead of assuming sharing is always better.

lec05kp12en-u01-p15-title.name: u01-p15-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p15-title.text: Extension: count parameters for an eight-by-eight image

lec05kp12en-u01-p15-bridge.name: u01-p15-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p15-bridge.text: The postal-code example combines local windows with corresponding shared connections. If our toy image grows, which counts change?

lec05kp12en-u01-p15-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-kernel
lec05kp12en-u01-p15-fig1.text: 重用的3乘3權重矩陣，中欄為1，其餘為0，偏置為0。

image.alt: Reusable three-by-three kernel with ones in its center column, zeros elsewhere and bias zero.

lec05kp12en-u01-p15-card1.name: u01-p15-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p15-card1.text: Question 1: use an 8×8 input, 3×3 window, stride one, no padding and a shared bias. Find map size and shared versus unshared counts.

lec05kp12en-u01-p15-card2.name: u01-p15-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p15-card2.text: Question 2: high responses follow an input shift. Is this equivariance or invariance? Compare $F(Tx)=TF(x)$ with $F(Tx)=F(x)$.

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-title.name: u01-p16-title
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-title.text: Extension: a six-by-six map still shares only ten parameters

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-bridge.name: u01-p16-bridge
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-bridge.text: Question 1 changes map size and parameter count; question 2 distinguishes equivariance from invariance. What do the steps give?

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-next-question.name: u01-p16-next-question
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-next-question.text: Can you recompute an example and state its limits?

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp12-maps-practice
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-fig1.text: 8乘8輸入的練習產生6乘6特徵圖，平移前後最大值都為3。

image.alt: Two six-by-six feature maps from eight-by-eight inputs; response maxima shift by two columns and both remain three.

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-card1.name: u01-p16-card1
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-card1.text: 1. Each direction has $8-3+1=6$ positions, giving $6\times6=36$: a 6×6 map.

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-card2.name: u01-p16-card2
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-card2.text: 2. Without sharing: $36\times(9+1)=360$. With sharing: $9+1=10$. A larger image adds uses, not parameters in this shared kernel.

lec05kp12en-u01-p16-card3.name: u01-p16-card3
lec05kp12en-u01-p16-card3.text: 3. A moving response is equivariance; suitable aggregation under the required conditions can yield an invariant feature.

Count the orange patch's three rows and columns, then compute six minus three plus one positions. The receptive field is not the whole image.
Next page: A receptive field sees nine numbers at each of sixteen positions. Can those positions reuse one set of weights?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 2: Each position first examines a small local patch.

steps.label: Reuse a kernel
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Each position first examines a small local patch.
The unflipped-kernel operation is cross-correlation, commonly called convolution in deep learning. The score 3 is neither class 3 nor a probability.
Next page: One reusable set of nine weights gives a local feature score. How do we organize scores while retaining positions?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 3: Reuse one set of nine weights at every window.

steps.label: Feature map
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Reuse one set of nine weights at every window.
Locate the value 3 in both maps and relate it to the original stroke. Localization is useful in detection and segmentation tasks.
Next page: The feature map retains local responses by position. Both maxima are three at different locations: is the map itself unchanged?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 4: Arrange local scores into a feature map.

steps.label: Equivariance
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Arrange local scores into a feature map.
Clarify the source's phrase identical response: corresponding local computations agree, not every fixed-position output.
Next page: Translation equivariance gives a correspondingly translated response. How can classification discard position while retaining the feature?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 5: Shared weights usually make responses move with the input.

steps.label: Pool for invariance
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Shared weights usually make responses move with the input.
One equality is not a theorem for every image or translation. Cropping, occlusion, stride and boundaries can break the assumptions.
Next page: Global max pooling retains the same scalar in this example. How many adjustable numbers does sharing also save?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 6: Aggregating over position can create an invariant feature.

steps.label: Count shared values
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Aggregating over position can create an invariant feature.
Biases are shared too; position-specific biases would change the count. Distinguish parameter storage, uses and arithmetic operations.
Next page: Sharing uses just nine weights and one bias across sixteen positions. How should one shared value receive updates from every position?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 7: Sharing across sixteen positions reduces one hundred sixty parameters to ten.

steps.label: Sum shared gradients
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Sharing across sixteen positions reduces one hundred sixty parameters to ten.
Uses contribute additively rather than overwriting the parameter. If loss is averaged, delta already carries that scaling; do not divide again arbitrarily.
Next page: A shared weight accumulates gradients from every use. What other approaches complement architecture constraints for transformation stability?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 8: A shared weight accumulates gradients from every use.

steps.label: Three routes
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: A shared weight accumulates gradients from every use.
The routes can be combined. Rotating a six into a nine can change the class; first check whether the transformation preserves labels.
Next page: Invariant features, architectural constraints and data augmentation can be combined. How can architecture also represent products of pixels?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 9: Invariant features, architectural constraints and augmentation are different routes.

steps.label: Pairwise products
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Invariant features, architectural constraints and augmentation are different routes.
Order refers to the degree of input products, not network depth. This is a second-order example, not a name for all deep networks.
Next page: A higher-order network weights products of pixels. Which geometric quantity of a pixel pair is preserved by translation?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 10: Higher-order networks also weight products of pixels.

steps.label: Share displacement
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Higher-order networks also weight products of pixels.
This corrects the source's translation description. Slope-only tying may impose extra constraints, but slope does not identify translation-equivalent segments.
Next page: Pure translation preserves displacement, not merely slope. Which segment property survives rotation and suggests a different tying rule?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 11: Pure translation preserves displacement, not merely slope.

steps.label: Share length
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Pure translation preserves displacement, not merely slope.
Ordinary translation-shared kernels do not automatically guarantee rotation invariance. The grouping rules represent different symmetries.
Next page: Rotation preserves segment length, subject to grid conditions. What single shared squared-norm coefficient does the circular model add?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 12: Rotation preserves length, subject to grid and model conditions.

steps.label: Circular model
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Rotation preserves length, subject to grid and model conditions.
Orthogonal vector rotations and sampled image rotations are distinct. The two-point counterexample separates an invariant term from an invariant classifier.
Next page: An invariant squared-norm term is not an invariant classifier. How did the source postal-code network organize first-order sharing?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 13: A shared squared-norm term does not make the whole model invariant.

steps.label: Postal-code example
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: A shared squared-norm term does not make the whole model invariant.
Ask which toy assumptions fail for real glyphs: width, style, borders and rotations. This transfers better than memorizing one layer count.
Next page: The postal-code example combines local windows with corresponding shared connections. If our toy image grows, which counts change?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 14: The postal-code example combines locality and shared weights.

steps.label: Extension: practice
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: The postal-code example combines locality and shared weights.
Count nine weights and one bias per position before multiplying. For question 2 distinguish the whole array from a pooled scalar.
Next page: Question 1 changes map size and parameter count; question 2 distinguishes equivariance from invariance. What do the steps give?
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 15: Extension: count parameters for an eight-by-eight image.

steps.label: Extension: answers
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Extension: count parameters for an eight-by-eight image.
Close by shifting the stroke out of the image: the maximum need not survive because the feature-preservation condition has failed.
Next page: Return to the practice and state the assumptions in your own words.
Source: Ch04 KP12, 4.11; focus 16: Extension: a six-by-six map still shares only ten parameters.
